postureDetail.at-risk: A check fails and its grace period has not ended.
postureDetail.non-compliant: A check fails that blocks, or its grace period ended.
postureDetail.pending: osquery has not answered every check yet. The checks run every 15 minutes.

checkDetail.disk-encryption: FileVault, BitLocker on C:, or LUKS under /
checkDetail.os-version: At least the minimum the policy sets for macOS, Windows and each Linux distribution
checkDetail.firewall: The macOS application firewall, or Windows Defender Firewall; not checked on Linux
checkDetail.screen-lock: A password within the policy's minutes on macOS, the inactivity limit on Windows; not checked on Linux

welcomePage.title: Get started
welcomePage.description: No device has enrolled yet. Each laptop and workstation runs osquery with Endpoints' query pack, and sends what it finds here.
welcomePage.step1: Under Enrolment, an admin makes an enrolment secret.
welcomePage.step2: Install osquery on a device from osquery.io.
welcomePage.step3: Put the three files next to it: osquery.flags, osquery.conf and enroll_secret, and start osquery.
welcomePage.step4: The device shows here at once; its checks within 15 minutes and its software within an hour.
welcomePage.askAdmin: Ask an admin of this Endpoints to make an enrolment secret.
welcomePage.readOnly: The queries are in the pack on each device. Endpoints never sends a device a query or a command, and cannot lock, wipe or change one.

devicesPage.title: Devices
devicesPage.outdatedPackTitle: Some devices run an older query pack
devicesPage.outdatedPack_one: {{count}} device runs another pack than version {{version}}. Put the osquery.conf from Enrolment on it.
devicesPage.outdatedPack_other: {{count}} devices run another pack than version {{version}}. Put the osquery.conf from Enrolment on them.

devicePage.checksDetail: From the last answer of each query; a failing check's grace period starts when it began to fail.
devicePage.exceptionDetail: The check counts as passing on this device until the exception ends. It is recorded with your name and the reason.
devicePage.reasonPlaceholder: Lab machine on an isolated network
devicePage.usersDetail: The accounts people sign in with on this device.
devicePage.name: Name
devicePage.reenrolDetail: Until {{date}}, osquery on this hardware may enrol once more, as after a reinstall. Its old node key stops working then.
devicePage.removeDetail: What it reported is deleted and its node key stops working. While its enrolment secret is valid, osquery on it enrols again as a new device: revoke the secret or uninstall osquery to stop it.

compliancePage.title: Compliance
compliancePage.description: The checks every device must pass, and the devices that fail them
compliancePage.checksDetail: Select a check to see the devices that fail it
compliancePage.notCheckedDetail: Devices it does not apply to, and devices osquery has not answered for yet.
compliancePage.onFailureDetail: Blocks at once makes the device non-compliant at once. A grace period leaves it at risk for the policy's days first.

softwarePage.title: Software
softwarePage.description: Applications and packages on every device, from osquery's apps, programs, deb_packages and rpm_packages
softwarePage.behindDetail: Devices without the newest version any device has. A sign, not an advisory.
softwarePage.noneDetail: osquery sends each device's software within an hour of enrolling.
softwarePage.pickDetail: Select an application to see its versions and where it is installed.

policyPage.title: Policy
policyPage.description: What a compliant device is. The defaults until an admin changes them.
policyPage.updated: What a compliant device is · changed by {{by}}, {{when}}
policyPage.minLinuxHint: Distribution and version, as osquery names them: ubuntu 22.04, debian 12. Others are not checked.
policyPage.checksDetail: Which checks count, and what a failure does
policyPage.saved: Saved. Every device was checked again against what it last reported.
policyPage.exceptionsDetail: Approved deviations with an end date; admins add them on a device's page
policyPage.noExceptionsDetail: Every device is held to the policy.

setupPage.title: Enrolment
setupPage.description: How a laptop or workstation starts reporting: osquery, the query pack and an enrolment secret
setupPage.https: ENDPOINTS_PUBLIC_URL is {{url}}. Put Endpoints behind a TLS proxy and set its https:// address, or devices cannot reach it.
setupPage.secretsDetail: Many devices enrol with one secret until it expires or is revoked; each then has a node key of its own. A secret is shown once.
setupPage.made: It is not shown again. Save it as enroll_secret next to osquery.flags on each device.
setupPage.noSecretsAdmin: Make one above to enrol devices.
setupPage.noSecretsDetail: An admin makes one to enrol devices.
setupPage.deviceDetail: Three files and osquery's own installer
setupPage.step2: Download osquery.flags and osquery.conf here, and save the enrolment secret as enroll_secret.
setupPage.step3: Run the commands below, or roll the three files out with your device management.
setupPage.proxyCa: If the proxy in front of Endpoints uses a certificate of your own CA, add --tls_server_certs with that CA's file to osquery.flags.
setupPage.packDetail: Everything osquery reads for Endpoints, in osquery.conf on each device. Endpoints cannot send a device any other query.

auditPage.title: Audit log
auditPage.description: Every enrolment, refused enrolment, change and sign-in. Rows are never changed or removed.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Endpoints.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this Endpoints, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also set who uses a device; admins also keep the policy, exceptions and enrolment secrets, remove devices, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and a SIEM. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
